english: Let $C$ be the parabola whose focus is $S(1,2)$ and whose directrix is the line $x=-2$. Let $V$ be the vertex of $C$ and let $L$ be the end of the latus rectum of $C$ that lies in the first quadrant. The circle described on $VL$ as a diameter meets the $y$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$. If $O$ is the origin, then the value of $OA\cdot OB$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ वह परवलय है जिसकी नाभि $S(1,2)$ है तथा जिसकी नियता रेखा $x=-2$ है। माना कि $V$, $C$ का शीर्ष है तथा $L$, $C$ के नाभिलम्ब का वह सिरा है जो प्रथम चतुर्थांश में स्थित है। $VL$ को व्यास मानकर खींचा गया वृत्त $y$-अक्ष को बिन्दुओं $A$ तथा $B$ पर मिलता है। यदि $O$ मूलबिन्दु है, तो $OA\cdot OB$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Axis $y=2$; foot of directrix $Z(-2,2)$; $V$ = midpoint of $ZS=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},2\right)$; $a=VS=\dfrac{3}{2}$
Latus rectum $=4a=6$, ends $(1,2\pm3)$; in the first quadrant $L(1,5)$
$x=0$: $y^{2}-7y+\dfrac{19}{2}=0$, discriminant $49-38=11>0$; sum $7>0$, product $\dfrac{19}{2}>0$, so $A,B$ are on the positive $y$-axis
solution_full: The axis of $C$ is the line through $S(1,2)$ perpendicular to the directrix $x=-2$, i.e. $y=2$. It meets the directrix at $Z(-2,2)$.
The vertex is the midpoint of $ZS$: $V=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},2\right)$, and $a=VS=\dfrac{3}{2}$. (So $C:\ (y-2)^{2}=6\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.)

The latus rectum is the focal chord perpendicular to the axis, of length $4a=6$, so its ends are $(1,2+3)=(1,5)$ and $(1,2-3)=(1,-1)$. The end in the first quadrant is $L(1,5)$. Check: $(5-2)^{2}=9=6\left(1+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.
The circle with $V\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},2\right)$ and $L(1,5)$ as ends of a diameter is $\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(x-1)+(y-2)(y-5)=0$, i.e. $x^{2}+y^{2}-\dfrac{1}{2}x-7y+\dfrac{19}{2}=0$.

On the $y$-axis ($x=0$): $y^{2}-7y+\dfrac{19}{2}=0$. Its discriminant is $49-38=11>0$, so there are two points $A$ and $B$, with $y_{A}+y_{B}=7$ and $y_{A}y_{B}=\dfrac{19}{2}$. Both roots are positive, so $OA=y_{A}$ and $OB=y_{B}$.
Hence $OA\cdot OB=\dfrac{19}{2}=9.5$. (This is also the power of $O$ with respect to the circle, the constant term $\dfrac{19}{2}$.)
originality_note: New: a circle whose diameter joins two elements of a parabola given by focus and directrix (vertex and one end of the latus rectum), read through the power of the origin (way 5). Closest known: 'circle described on the latus rectum (or a focal chord) as diameter touches the directrix'. Different because: the diameter VL is not a focal chord, so no standard property applies; the elements must be located and the product of intercepts read from the diametric equation.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard parabola:: The axis, the foot of the directrix, the vertex V (midpoint of ZS), a = 3/2 and the latus-rectum end L(1, 5) are read from the focus and directrix.
concept_use.Diametrical form of circle: The circle on VL as diameter is written in diametric form (x - x1)(x - x2) + (y - y1)(y - y2) = 0, and its y-intercepts give OA·OB.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that the latus-rectum end in the first quadrant is unique (L(1, 5); the other end (1, -1) is in the fourth quadrant), that the circle meets the y-axis at two distinct points on the positive side, and that 9.50 is a positive decimal as planned. Changed: specified 'in the first quadrant' for L, since otherwise two circles are possible.
key_step: Locating V and L from focus and directrix and writing the diametric circle.
justification: Routine chain: elements of a shifted parabola, diametric form of a circle, product of roots. Like 2026-P1-Q2 (L2), which builds a circle from points obtained on conics; above the one-step circle anchor 2024-P1-Q15 (L1).
